message.content:
There are 90 two-digit numbers: from 10 to 99.

Half of them are odd, so there are 45 odd two-digit numbers.

The product is **even unless both chosen numbers are odd**. So we compute the complement:

\[
P(\text{product even})=1-P(\text{both numbers odd})
\]

Choosing two different two-digit numbers from 90 total:

\[
P(\text{both odd})=\frac{\binom{45}{2}}{\binom{90}{2}}
=\frac{45\cdot 44}{90\cdot 89}
=\frac{22}{89}
\]

Thus,

\[
P(\text{product even})=1-\frac{22}{89}
=\frac{67}{89}
\]

The answer is \(\boxed{\frac{67}{89}}\).
